title: From Spectral Singularities to Multipartite Entanglement Scaling at Higher-Order Exceptional Points
authors: Chunlai Yang, Shuheng Liu, Xinyao Huang, Kaiye Shi, Qiongyi He
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) are non-Hermitian spectral singularities exhibiting fractional-power responses, yet their implications for multipartite entanglement of interacting quantum many-body systems remain largely unexplored. Here we develop a general framework that links higher-order non-Hermitian degeneracies to the scaling behavior of genuine multipartite entanglement in interacting identical-qubit systems. Permutation symmetry of the identical qubits decomposes the exponentially large Hilbert space into independent irreducible-representation sectors, thereby constraining the maximal EP order of $N$ qubits to $N+1$ rather than $2^N$. Near an $n$th-order EP, genuine multipartite entanglement inherits the spectral response and generically exhibits a fractional-power scaling under weak perturbations. Explicit examples show that conventional two-body interactions support third- and fourth-order EPs with the corresponding entanglement responses, whereas higher-order EPs with genuine multipartite-entangled coalesced states require additional independent interaction channels, such as three-body interactions. Our results establish a fundamental connection among non-Hermitian degeneracies, multipartite entanglement, and symmetry, extending higher-order EP physics from spectral singularities to genuine many-body quantum correlations.
summary: This theoretical paper connects higher-order Exceptional Points (EPs) in non-Hermitian systems to the behavior of genuine multipartite entanglement (GME). By exploiting permutation symmetry, the authors derive a general framework showing that GME exhibits a characteristic fractional-power scaling directly proportional to the inverse order of the EP. This establishes a fundamental link between spectral degeneracies and quantum correlations.
main_problem: The research aims to develop a general theoretical framework linking higher-order non-Hermitian degeneracies (Exceptional Points, EPs) to the scaling behavior of genuine multipartite entanglement (GME). It seeks to establish a fundamental connection between these concepts in interacting quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The study shows that GME inherits the spectral nonanalyticity near an $n$-th order EP, exhibiting a characteristic fractional-power scaling ($\Delta C \propto \delta^{1/n}$). Furthermore, it establishes that realizing higher-order EPs requires specific multi-body interaction channels.
method: The analysis utilizes permutation symmetry to decompose the Hilbert space of identical qubits and then analyzes the spectral response near an EP using perturbation theory, leading to a Puiseux series expansion for both energy eigenvalues and entanglement measures.
model_or_system: The model consists of interacting identical-qubit systems governed by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian $\hat{H}$, which includes single-qubit terms and arbitrary $l$-body interaction terms (e.g., XYZ Heisenberg interactions). The system's structure is constrained by permutation symmetry.
key_observables: Genuine Multipartite Entanglement (GME), spectral response, fractional-power scaling ($\delta^{1/n}$).
important_parameters: The order of the Exceptional Point ($n$), the number of qubits ($N$), and the strength of weak perturbations ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The Hamiltonian is assumed to preserve permutation symmetry; the analysis focuses on the leading-order scaling behavior near the EP.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the connection between interacting identical-qubit systems, the block-diagonal structure imposed by permutation symmetry, and the resulting fractional-power response of multipartite entanglement near an EP.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces EPs in non-Hermitian physics. It then leverages permutation symmetry to constrain the Hilbert space and analyze the system's degeneracy limit ($N+1$). The core is developing the framework linking this degeneracy structure directly to the scaling law of GME under weak perturbations, concluding with explicit examples requiring higher-order interactions.
why_interesting: This work bridges spectral theory (non-Hermitian physics) and quantum information theory (entanglement), providing a powerful diagnostic tool: measuring entanglement scaling can reveal the underlying degeneracy order of the system's Hamiltonian.
